assets.content:
Subject: Which referrers are tied to completed trial signups?
Preview text: With a distinct confirmation URL, a pageview goal can also show entry pages.

Hi there,

Plausible Analytics can track completed trial signups as a goal, then show which referrer sources and entry pages are associated with those conversions.

First, check whether a successful signup reaches a distinct confirmation URL. Once Plausible is collecting pageviews on the site, that URL can become a pageview goal without another code change.

After conversions are recorded, filtering the dashboard by that goal can show its conversion count and rate, referrer sources, entry pages and the top pages where people convert.

Inspect the official goal-conversions guide to decide whether a pageview goal fits your signup flow.

- the Plausible Analytics team

brief.reader_segment: Small SaaS website owner measuring signup conversion
brief.promise: Plausible can turn a trial signup into a conversion goal, then show which referrer sources and entry pages are associated with those conversions.
brief.orientation: Plausible Analytics is a web analytics tool that lets a SaaS owner measure trial signups as goals and examine the traffic that converted.
brief.arc: Introduce the specific signup-measurement use case, give one low-complexity first step, explain the resulting dashboard view, then invite the reader to verify the setup in the official guide.
brief.sequence_rationale: The audience is solution-aware, so the email should begin with the concrete job rather than explain why conversions matter. A pageview goal provides the clearest first step when signup ends on a distinct confirmation page; the official guide is the appropriate low-friction CTA because it documents goal setup and measurement without requiring an account commitment. No broader objection is staged because the request calls for one concise introduction.

emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the official guide and decide whether a pageview goal fits their trial-signup flow.
emails.single_idea: If a successful trial signup reaches a distinct confirmation page, that page can be defined as a pageview goal so Plausible can report signup conversions and the sources and landing pages behind them.
emails.felt_need: Free-trial signups do not convert to paid at a rate the owner considers acceptable, even after a signup surge.
emails.status_quo: They add free trials that require a payment method upfront to try to convert website visitors into paying customers.
emails.why_it_fails: A site-wide conversion rate alone does not identify which referrer sources or entry pages are associated with the signups.
emails.mechanism: First identify the URL shown after a completed trial signup. Once Plausible is collecting pageviews on the site, use that URL as a pageview goal; pageview goals require no additional code changes. After conversions are recorded, filtering the dashboard by that goal can show its conversion count and rate, referrer sources, entry pages and top converting pages.
emails.belief_shift: Before: signup measurement sounds like a broad analytics project. After: the reader sees a concrete first check—whether the signup confirmation URL can serve as a pageview goal—and knows what attribution the dashboard can then expose.
must_not_say: Do not presume the reader currently uses Plausible or any other analytics tool.
Do not presume traffic volume, privacy compliance status, a recent launch, or poor conversion performance.
Do not claim that installing Plausible or creating a goal will increase signups or produce any measured lift.
Do not present Plausible’s own conversion figures as a benchmark or expected result for the reader.
Do not claim this setup measures trial-to-paid conversion, failed payments, billing state or in-product trial usage.
Do not imply a pageview goal fits every signup flow; it depends on a distinct page or URL being reached after signup.
Do not lead with pricing, privacy, competitor comparisons, testimonials, uptime, integrations or the broader feature set.
Do not ask the reader to start a trial, view a demo or take any action other than inspecting the official goal-conversions guide.

Plausible can only record a paid conversion if the owner sends it as a backend event, revenue attribution sits on the Business plan, and the ledger contains nothing about in-trial product usage or billing, so the measurement stops at.

The 2.65% to 4.80% lift (E11) came from Plausible editing its own homepage, not from installing Plausible; the product locates entry pages and drop-off steps and the owner still has to make the change and re-measure.
emails.objection: Will measuring a signup require another code change? For a flow with a distinct confirmation URL, the pageview-goal step itself does not require one once Plausible is collecting pageviews.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the trial signup should be measured with a pageview goal based on a distinct confirmation URL.
emails.next_step_value: The guide explains how conversion goals work and how pageview goals can be set up and measured, including the conversion, source and entry-page insights available afterward.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the guide does not configure the reader’s site, establish a suitable benchmark, prove a conversion lift, or measure downstream paid conversion.
emails.subject_strategy: Name the practical task—seeing where trial signups come from—without implying a problem, result or existing analytics setup.

brief.voice_notes: Use short, declarative sentences and the product terms “goal,” “pageview goal,” “referrer sources,” “entry pages” and “dashboard.” Avoid hype and the phrase “Get started.”
